To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pancreatic tissue fragments transplants into the anterior eye chamber contain acetylcholinestrase- and monoamine oxidase- positive neuronal elements in the surviving and new islets of Langanhan, in the wall of the ducts and in their peripheral zone.
the embryonic pancreatic tissue, transplanted into eye-chamber, is able to regenerate and to maintain the neuronal elements.
acetylcholinestease-and monoamine-oxidase-positive neurons are found in the surviving and new islet cells, in the wall of ductules and periphery of pancreatic tubules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of MAO--and AChE--positive neurons in embryonic pancreatic fragments transplanted to the eye-chamber of adult rats.
the distribution of AChE-and MAO-positive neurons in pancreatic tissue fragments transplants.
the distribution and the possible role of MAO- and AChE-positive neuronal elements in the pancreatic tissue transplant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the neuronal components of the pancreas survive transplantation and that they have a topographical relationship to parenchymal cells similar to that in the native pancreas. A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pancreatic islet cells are able to regenerate in a new site, and that the MAO- and AChE-positive neuronal elements are also capable of regeneration, and that they are able to form a network of fibres around the ductal and the newly formed islets.
the embryonic pancreatic tissue, transplanted into anterior eye-chamber, preserves its neuronal components and that these cells are capable of synthesizing ACh and catecholamines.
the neuronal elements are present in the surviving and new formed islets of the pancreatic tissue fragments transplants, and their topography is similar to that found in normal tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pancreatic islets are able to survive and develop in an extrapancreatic site, in a manner which is not significantly different from that of normal pancreatic tissue.
the pancreatic tissue transplanted in the anterior eye-chambers of rats, is capable of forming a new neuronal tissue.
embryonic pancreatic tissue can survive in the anterior eye-chambers for a relatively long period and can be used for further studies.
